principles.statement: Document decisions and their reasons, not just mechanics — the 'why' is the part that cannot be re-derived from the code.
principles.rationale: The code shows what it does; six months later, only the doc can say why it does it that way and what alternatives were rejected.

principles.statement: Docs live next to the thing they describe and update in the same change.
principles.rationale: A separate docs repo drifts silently; a doc that must change with the code gets changed with the code or the same PR fails review.

principles.statement: Write for the reader who has the least context the doc assumes.
principles.rationale: Docs written by the just-finished-it author always assume too much; the target reader is someone returning in six months.

heuristics.name: Start with a working example
heuristics.description: One copy-paste-runnable example teaches more than three paragraphs of prose.
examples: A curl line beats an abstract description of the endpoint's semantics.

heuristics.name: Delete-or-date stale docs
heuristics.description: On finding a wrong doc: correct it if quick, otherwise mark it stale with a date — a wrong doc is worse than none.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Any time a doc contradicts current reality.
examples: 'NOTE: pre-2026-09 design, superseded by X' stops the doc from lying.

decision_rules.condition: A doc and the code disagree.
decision_rules.action: The code is current by definition — fix the doc immediately, and ask why the process let them diverge.

decision_rules.condition: A concept requires more than one paragraph of background before the main point.
decision_rules.action: Move the background to a linked reference doc; keep the main doc on the main point.
